title: Energy from fuels
bigPicture: Fuels store chemical energy that combustion releases as heat. Complete and incomplete combustion give different products, fossil fuels and biofuels differ in how much CO₂ they add and how renewable they are, and fuel cells turn a fuel's energy straight into electricity.

keyIdeas.answer: Reactive metals, non-metals and organic compounds burn in oxygen: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO; S + O₂ → SO₂. Complete combustion of hydrocarbons and alcohols gives CO₂ and H₂O: C₂H₅OH + 3O₂ → 2CO₂ + 3H₂O.

With limited oxygen, hydrocarbons and alcohols form carbon monoxide (toxic: binds to haemoglobin) and/or carbon (soot), plus water: 2CH₄ + 3O₂ → 2CO + 4H₂O; CH₄ + O₂ → C + 2H₂O. Larger hydrocarbons burn incompletely more easily.

Coal, crude oil and natural gas: high energy density and established infrastructure, but non-renewable and release CO₂ (a greenhouse gas: absorbs IR re-emitted by Earth). Coal releases most CO₂ per kJ and more pollutants (SO₂, particulates); natural gas the least. Compare using energy per gram and CO₂ per kJ.

Fuels from recently fixed carbon (photosynthesis: 6CO₂ + 6H₂O → C₆H₁₂O₆ + 6O₂), e.g. ethanol from fermentation, biodiesel. Renewable and close to carbon-neutral over a short cycle, but compete with food for land, need water and fertiliser, and have lower energy density.

keyIdeas.cue: How does a fuel cell work?
keyIdeas.answer: Fuel and oxygen are supplied continuously and react at separate electrodes, converting chemical energy directly to electrical energy. Hydrogen (acidic): anode H₂ → 2H⁺ + 2e⁻; cathode O₂ + 4H⁺ + 4e⁻ → 2H₂O. Methanol: anode CH₃OH + H₂O → CO₂ + 6H⁺ + 6e⁻; cathode 3/2O₂ + 6H⁺ + 6e⁻ → 3H₂O. Proton-exchange membrane details are not assessed.

keyTerms.def: Burning in excess oxygen: CO₂ and H₂O from organic fuels.
Burning in limited oxygen: CO and/or C form.
Energy released per unit mass of fuel (kJ g⁻¹).
Gas that absorbs and re-emits infrared radiation (CO₂, CH₄, H₂O).
Fuel made from biological material via recent photosynthesis.
Cell converting a fuel's chemical energy directly into electricity.

workedExamples.title: Energy per gram and CO₂ per kJ
workedExamples.prompt: Compare methane (ΔHc −891 kJ mol⁻¹, M 16.05) and octane (ΔHc −5470 kJ mol⁻¹, M 114.26).
steps: Energy per gram: methane 891/16.05 = 55.5 kJ g⁻¹; octane 5470/114.26 = 47.9 kJ g⁻¹.
CO₂ per 1000 kJ: methane 1 mol per 891 kJ → 1.12 mol; octane 8 mol per 5470 kJ → 1.46 mol.
workedExamples.answer: Methane releases more energy per gram and less CO₂ per kJ.

misconceptions.wrong: Biofuels add no CO₂ to the atmosphere.
misconceptions.right: They release CO₂ when burned, but it was absorbed recently; farming and processing add more, so they're not fully carbon-neutral.
There is no flame; oxidation and reduction happen at separate electrodes.
It releases less energy per mole of fuel than complete combustion.
